newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields edge higher post-tender.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields edge higher post-tender.

text.p: Australian bond yields edged higher in the aftermath of Tuesday's A$500 million two tranche tender, which was described as reasonable, but unlikely to stir too much interest in the market.
"I think you are seeing some consolidation post-tender, but I think it sums up the current lack of interest in the market," said one trader.
At 2.20 p.m. (0420 GMT) the September 10-year bond futures contract was 93.480 compared to 93.500 at the 12.30 p.m. (0230 GMT) recess.
However, given the relatively small size of the tender and recent liquidity tightness in the market, traders doubted that the mildly negative tone would persist too long.

The A$200 million of October 2007 stock, the current 10-year benchmark, went off at a weighted average yield of 6.508 percent compared with around 6.52/6.48 percent seen quoted when final bids went in and an accepted bid range of 6.50 to 6.51 percent.

The A$300 million of the longer September 2009 stock fetched a yield of 6.597 percent with bids ranging from 6.58 to 6.60 percent. The stock was quoted at around 6.60/6.56 percent when tender bids went in.
This was the first tender for the 1997/98 fiscal year and the first since April 8 when the October 2007 stock was then also offered.
The weighted average yield then was 7.958 percent, highlighting the extent of the rally since.

This rally, which saw the 10-year bond yield below 6.40 percent for the first time since the early 1980s last week, has largely been inspired by expectations of a further easing in monetary policy, which is expected to become a reality at next week's Reserve Bank board meeting.
At the May budget the Treasury projected fixed interest debt issuance at A$5.0 to A$6.0 billion for the 1997/98 fiscal year.

"Our understanding is that there are going to be ten tenders of A$500 million a time, and if that's the case it looks fairly tame and should help smooth shortages over the course of the year," another trader added.
